About Me

Engineered for Performance, Scalability & Precision

I am a Computer Engineering student at Alamein International University (AIU) with a strong focus on data engineering, analytical architecture, and backend software development. My experience spans designing end-to-end relational data warehouses (including Medallion Architectures and Star Schema models), optimizing SQL performance, and building clean, modular software.

Whether constructing ETL pipelines, optimizing query performance with targeted indexing, or developing structured applications in Python, Java, or C++, I prioritize system reliability, clean code, and measurable real-world outcomes.

Enterprise Retail Data Warehouse

Architecture & Deep Dive

Built a retail data warehouse that turns raw transactional sales records into an analytics-ready Star Schema using a Medallion architecture.

  • Medallion architecture separating raw staging from the star schema gold layer
  • One central fact table (fact_sales) linked to five dimensions: date, ship mode, customer, product and geography
  • Reduced execution time of monthly KPI reports by over 40%
View Repository

Bank Management System

Java OOP, GUI & Database

Built a banking application in Java that combines object-oriented design, a graphical user interface, and a database layer, so bank data persists between sessions instead of living only in memory.

  • Object-oriented class design separating business logic from the interface and data access
  • Graphical user interface that lets users interact with the system without a command line
  • Database integration for storing and retrieving bank records reliably
View Repository

RFM Customer Segmentation

Data Analytics & Customer Behavior

Not all customers are equally valuable. This project applies RFM analysis to a customer transactions dataset: measuring how recently each customer purchased, how often they purchase, and how much they spend, then grouping customers into five segments (A, B, C, D and F) so marketing effort can be focused where it matters.

  • Calculated Recency, Frequency and Monetary metrics per customer
  • Scored each customer and assigned them to one of five segments (A, B, C, D, F)
  • Segment B is the largest group and segment F the smallest, giving a clear view of where the customer base sits
